scope: Visual review of six sampled PNG frames from the final daytime connecting-flight movie, focused on museum approach and interior framing. Full video timing and decoding were handled separately by the parent.

images.finding: Garden-to-museum establishing view: Modern Wing, roof and Nichols Bridgeway are recognizable behind the planting; no foreground object blocks the overall museum approach.
Modern Wing is centered at a useful scale. Roof blades, glazed pavilion levels and the central entry court are readable; bridge remains visible on the right.
Ground approach frames the central entrance and long court. Thin façade members cross the image as expected, but the entry opening and interior remain visible.
Inside Griffin Court, the camera has a clear forward corridor between the slender columns. Floor, wall planes and skylight rhythm remain readable.
The turn presents the gallery opening, bench and framed artwork. Foreground architectural columns remain visible without filling or blocking the view.
Final gallery composition clearly frames three original geometric artworks, neutral walls, plaster ceiling, floor and wall labels. Exposure and caption readability are satisfactory.

limitations: This is sampled-frame review, not a claim that every intervening movie frame was individually inspected.
Fine sampling grain remains visible around glazing, thin members and some interior floor/ceiling regions.
The museum room, artworks, sculpture details and planting are authored interpretations; simplified architectural and landscape forms remain apparent.
